message.content:
**Civil law**—the body of legal norms governing private relationships between individuals or entities—is usually divided into two broad families: | Category | What it covers | Key elements | |----------|-----------------|--------------| | **Substantive law** – *what people owe each other* | • Contracts
• Torts (negligence, defamation, nuisance)
• Property rights (ownership, easements, leases)
• Family matters (marriage, divorce, child custody & support, adoption)
• Succession / wills & estates
• Consumer protection
• Employment relations (except labor‑union disputes which may fall under public law) | These rules define duties, liabilities, entitlements, and how they arise. | | **Procedural law** – *how disputes get resolved* | • Jurisdiction (which court has authority)
• Pleadings, motions, discovery, trial procedures
• Evidence rules (relevance, admissibility, hearsay exceptions)
• Remedies (damages, specific performance, rescission, injunctions)
• Appeals process | This framework tells parties what steps to take, when deadlines expire, who can hear their case, and how decisions can be challenged. | --- ### Core Components of Substantive Civil Law 1. **Contracts** - Offer, acceptance, consideration, capacity, legality, and breach consequences. 2. **Tort Law** - Duty of care → negligence; intentional wrongs → battery, assault, fraud; strict liability cases. 3. **Property Rights** - Real estate ownership, possession, transfer, mortgages, liens, eminent domain. 4. **Family Law** - Marriage dissolution, alimony, spousal support, child custody/visitation, child support, guardianship. 5. **Succession/Wills** - Testamentary dispositions, intestate succession statutes, probate proceedings. 6. **Consumer Protection** - Unfair trade practices, warranties, product safety regulations. 7. **Employment Relations** - Non‑discrimination, wage laws, wrongful termination claims (often mediated through administrative agencies). --- ### Core Components of Procedural Civil Law 1. **Jurisdiction & Venue** - Personal jurisdiction over defendants, subject‑matter jurisdiction, proper venue selection. 2. **Pleadings & Motions** - Complaint, answer, counterclaim, cross‑claim, summary judgment motion, dismissal requests. 3. **Discovery** - Interrogatories, depositions, document production, subpoenas, expert reports. 4. **Evidence Rules** - Relevancy, authenticity, privilege, hearsay exclusions, burden of proof (“preponderance of evidence”). 5. **Trial Process** - Jury vs bench trials, opening statements, witness examination, closing arguments. 6. **Remedies** - Compensatory damages, punitive damages, nominal damages, injunctive relief, declaratory judgments. 7. **Appeals** - Standard of review (de novo, abuse of discretion, clearly erroneous), appellate briefs, oral argument. --- ### How It All Fits Together A typical civil dispute follows this flow: ``` [Contract signed] ➜ [Breach occurs] ↓ Filing a lawsuit ↓ Pre‑trial discovery ↓ Motion practice (summary judgment) ↓ Trial (jury or judge) ↓ Judgment (monetary award/injunction) ↓ Appeal (if necessary) ``` Each step relies on both substantive rules (e.g., “who owes whom”) and procedural rules (e.g., “when must you serve the defendant”). --- #### Quick Reference Checklist | Step | Question | Typical Rule(s) | |------|-----------|------------------| | Contract formation | Is there offer + acceptance + consideration? | UCC § 2–201, common‑law contract doctrine | | Breach | Did one party fail to perform? | Restatement (Second) of Contracts §§ 50‑55 | | Damages | Who suffered loss? | Common‑law compensatory damage formulas | | Tort claim | Was duty breached? | Negligence standard (reasonable person test) | | Discovery deadline | When does deposition occur? | Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 26(a)(1) | | Summary judgment | Does material fact exist? | FRCP 56(b) | | Injunction | Need immediate relief? | FRCP 65 | Feel free to ask if you'd like deeper detail on any particular component!
message.reasoning:
The user asks: "What are the components of Civil Law?" They want an explanation. No tool needed. Just answer.

We should provide overview: sources (statutes, case law), principles like contract, torts, property, family law, restitution, remedies, procedural aspects, courts, judges, juries, etc. Also mention civil procedure rules, evidence, damages, injunctions, arbitration, mediation. Provide structure maybe categories: substantive and procedural. So respond accordingly.
